mutation_targets.rationale: The permission matrix defines which roles are allowed to perform each operation. Removing this constraint leaves PermMatrix.Allowed unconstrained; without the closed-world definition, Alloy can choose an empty set of permissions, causing all assertions checking 'some role can perform operation X' to fail.

This fact enforces that all sharees must belong to the same team as the task owner (FR-012). Removing it allows Alloy to create cross-team shares, which directly violates the isolation requirement and permits information leakage to users in other teams.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamShare { some disj t: Task, u: User | u in t.shared_with and u.team != t.owner.team }

mutation_targets.rationale: This fact mandates that every task must have at least one audit entry, ensuring audit completeness (FR-015 and SC-007). Without it, Alloy can create tasks that never produced any audit trail, violating the invariant that every mutation must be recorded.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoAuditEntry { some t: Task | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.task = t }

mutation_targets.rationale: This fact ensures every task's owner belongs to the task's team, supporting the ownership-based access control model and cross-team isolation (FR-006). Removing it allows owners from other teams, breaking the invariant that tasks are scoped to a single team.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamOwner { some disj t: Task, u: User | t.owner = u and u.team != t.team }

mutation_targets.rationale: The permission matrix is the canonical source of what operations are permitted for each role. Clearing it (making Allowed empty) removes all role-operation allowances, directly falsifying assertions that check members can create tasks or admins can edit team tasks.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_EmptyPermMatrix { all r: Role, op: OperationKind | r -> op not in PermMatrix.Allowed }
